title: Aeroméxico 498
summary: Aeroméxico Flight 498 collided with a Piper PA-28 Cherokee that entered the Los Angeles Terminal Control Area without clearance. The Piper was not equipped with a Mode C transponder and was not visible to either crew or ATC radar. The DC-9 crashed in a residential neighborhood in Cerritos, killing 64 on the aircraft, 3 in the Piper, and 15 on the ground.
probable_cause: The limitations of the air traffic control system to provide collision protection, through both ATC procedures and automated redundancy. Contributing factors were the inadvertent and unauthorized entry of the PA-28 into the Los Angeles Terminal Control Area and the limitations of the 'see and avoid' concept to ensure traffic separation.

factors.evidence: Piper collided nearly perpendicular with DC-9, shearing top of Piper cockpit and damaging DC-9's tail surfaces; DC-9 crashed in Cerritos.
Neither pilot sighted the other aircraft; neither appeared to attempt evasive maneuvers.
Piper not equipped with Mode C transponder; LAX radar not equipped with automatic warning systems.
ATC was distracted by another unauthorized private aircraft (Grumman AA-5B Tiger) entering the Terminal Control Area.
Piper pilot entered the Los Angeles Terminal Control Area without required clearance; entry was inadvertent, not due to physiological disablement.

events.text: DC-9 Flight 498 begins descent into Los Angeles with 58 passengers and 6 crew.
Piper PA-28 collided nearly perpendicular with DC-9's upper left side of horizontal stabilizer support.
Collision sheared top of Piper's cockpit and severely damaged DC-9's tail surfaces including horizontal stabilizer, rudder, and vertical stabilizer.
DC-9 with damaged tail surfaces over-banked to right and entered steep dive; crashed in residential area of Cerritos.

recommendations.text: Expedite development, operational evaluation, and final certification of Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
Amend 14 CFR Parts 121 and 135 to require TCAS installation in certificated air carrier aircraft
Implement procedures to track, identify, and take enforcement action against pilots who intrude into ARSAs without ATC communications

notes: Sections read: Findings, Probable Cause, Recommendations
